entries.clue: Some paratha, ricotta and a kind of bean (7)

indicatorNotes.Some: only part of the following words is taken

blocks.note: the last two letters of paratha run on into the first five of ricotta

annotation.surface: An Indian-Italian plate: flatbread, soft cheese and some beans.
annotation.walkthrough: The food words around it are camouflage in a food-themed puzzle; the bean is sitting across the join between the bread and the cheese.
annotation.definitionFit: The haricot is the small white bean used for baked beans.

entries.clue: Rice and this curry can be arranged for Leonardo da Vinci! (8)

indicatorNotes.can be arranged for: the letters of rice, and and the answer can be rearranged to make the name

blocks.note: the full letter set: RICE + AND + the answer
the letters R, I, C, E, A, N, D are removed from the name's letter set; what remains is jumbled

annotation.surface: A playful claim that a curry order can be rearranged into the great Renaissance artist.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: RICE + AND + VINDALOO together rearrange to LEONARDO DA VINCI, so remove RICE and AND from the name and the remaining letters give the curry.
annotation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a hot curry, here pointed at by 'this'.

entries.clue: Booze; aroma: roses – or latterly, oak, primarily? (6)

annotation.definition: Booze; aroma: roses – or latterly, oak, primarily?

indicatorNotes.primarily: in the first place, so each word gives only its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: Booze; aroma: roses – or latterly, oak
blocks.note: B-ooze, A-roma, R-oses, O-r, L-atterly, O-ak

annotation.surface: A wine-tasting note: the drink smells of roses, with oak coming through at the end.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the wine: Barolo is often said to smell of roses, and is aged in oak.
annotation.definitionFit: Barolo is a red wine from Piedmont, so booze with a rose aroma and oak finish.

entries.clue: Mostly chocolatey dessert? In other words ... it includes lamb (8)

indicatorNotes.Mostly: most of the word, but not all of it, so the final letter is cut off

aka = also known as

annotation.surface: A menu description that trails off: a chocolate pudding, or rather, something with lamb in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In other words' looks like a connecting phrase but is the wordplay: AKA, 'also known as'.
annotation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a Greek baked dish of aubergine layered with minced lamb.

entries.clue: Form an attachment to rice, perhaps (6)

blocks.note: the office sense: fasten papers together with a bent wire
rice as an example of a basic food eaten every day

annotation.surface: Someone growing fond of rice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attachment' reads as emotional fondness; it is the office sense of fastening.
annotation.definitionFit: To staple is to fasten; a staple is a basic food such as rice.

entries.clue: Languish with idiot having assembled something for pasta sauce (4,3)

blocks.note: to pine = to languish
a nut = an idiot

annotation.surface: Someone moping about with a fool while putting together the makings of a pasta sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: The pasta sauce is pesto, whose ingredients include pine nuts.
annotation.definitionFit: Pine nuts are ground into pesto, a pasta sauce.

entries.clue: Note you'll hear: warmer Mexican fare (6)

a warmer is a heater; Spanish J is said like H, so JITA is said 'heeta'

annotation.surface: A menu note promising a hot Mexican dish.
annotation.walkthrough: FAJITA is said 'fa-HEE-ta', which is FA + HEATER in a non-rhotic accent.
annotation.definitionFit: A fajita is a Mexican dish of grilled meat in a tortilla.

entries.clue: I'm persuasive. Like a milkshake? (8)

blocks.note: the boast of a smooth-talking charmer
a thick blended fruit drink

annotation.surface: A drink boasting of its charm.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is spoken by the answer: a smoothie would say 'I'm persuasive'.
annotation.definitionFit: A smoothie is both a smooth operator and a blended drink resembling a milkshake.

entries.clue: I sailed oceans meandering to find Riviera speciality (6,7)

indicatorNotes.meandering: wandering about, so the letters move

annotation.surface: A traveller who wandered the seas in search of a Riviera dish.
annotation.walkthrough: The Riviera here is the French one, around Nice.
annotation.definitionFit: Salade niçoise, with tuna, egg, olives and beans, comes from Nice on the French Riviera.

entries.clue: Cryptic clue for wolf – or pheasant, perhaps (8)

blocks.note: the answer, read as a clue, is an anagram instruction whose result is WOLF
game birds

annotation.surface: A setter admitting how they would clue a wolf, or a pheasant.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer itself works as a clue: 'wild' can signal an anagram, and FOWL scrambled is WOLF.
annotation.definitionFit: Wildfowl are game birds such as pheasant and duck.

entries.clue: Meal measures up perfectly? To some extent (6)

indicatorNotes.To some extent: only part of the phrase is used

blocks.note: the last letter of measures, all of up, and the first three of perfectly

annotation.surface: Asking whether a meal was quite up to scratch, and hearing 'more or less'.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'To some extent' read as a hedge on the praise; they are the instruction to look inside the words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the answer is a light evening meal.

entries.clue: In Korean capital, lacking energy, scoff seeing sweet potato pie, etc (4,4)

indicatorNotes.lacking: the city is without energy, so the letter standing for energy goes missing from it

blocks.note: capital of South Korea
E = energy; taken out of SEOUL leaves SOUL
scoff is British slang for food

annotation.surface: A tired diner in Seoul, eating and noticing a Southern American dessert.
annotation.walkthrough: Scoff is used as a noun here: British slang for food. Soul food is the cooking of African Americans in the US South.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: sweet potato pie is one dish of the African-American Southern cuisine, and 'etc' widens it to the whole cuisine.

entries.clue: Singular hawker, we're told, dined – but not at home (3,3)

indicatorNotes.we're told: the words are to be heard, not read

blocks.note: a tout is someone who hawks tickets; 'singular' gives A

annotation.surface: A street seller telling how someone had a meal in a restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: A tout is a person who sells tickets for events at inflated prices outside the venue.
annotation.definitionFit: To eat out is to dine away from home, at a restaurant.

entries.clue: Old French president concealing origins of affaire involving starlet: sauce! (11)

indicatorNotes.concealing: the president holds the other letters inside
indicatorNotes.origins of: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: François Hollande, French president 2012–17
A-ffaire, I-nvolving, S-tarlet

annotation.surface: A gossip headline about a former French president hiding a fling with an actress – scandalous!
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sauce!' reads as an exclamation of cheek, in keeping with the scandal; it is the definition. 'Old' is needed because Hollande left office in 2017.
annotation.definitionFit: Hollandaise is a sauce of butter, egg yolk and lemon.

entries.clue: Initially lacking punch (initially lacking): long time to get something to eat (8)

indicatorNotes.Initially lacking: drop the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: first letter of lacking
PUNCH without its first letter
an eon is an age

annotation.surface: A weak drink and a long wait before the food arrives.
annotation.walkthrough: The bracketed repeat looks like a typo; it is a second instruction, taking the L from 'lacking' itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Luncheon is a formal word for lunch.

entries.clue: Not finishing various starters of Italian endives, dressed like some tomatoes (3-5)

I-talian, E-ndives, D-ressed

annotation.surface: An unfinished Italian salad of assorted endives, dressed as tomatoes are.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' sounds like the salad dressing but is only there for its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Describes a preparation: some tomatoes are left out in the heat until shrivelled, then kept in oil.

entries.clue: Attractive people that are often fuzzy and usually stoned (7)

fruit with downy skin and a stone

annotation.walkthrough: 'Fuzzy' and 'stoned' suggest drugged people; they describe the fruit's downy skin and its stone.
annotation.definitionFit: A peach is both a delightful person and a stone fruit with a fuzzy skin.

entries.clue: Ship that may contain broccoli (7)

blocks.note: a steamship
a pan for steaming vegetables

annotation.surface: A cargo vessel carrying vegetables.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a cargo of broccoli; the second steamer is the kitchen pan.
annotation.definitionFit: A steamer is a steamship and also a pan for steaming food.

entries.clue: With teetotaller absent, brunette prepared something with rye (6)

indicatorNotes.absent: the teetotaller is not present, so those letters leave the fodder
indicatorNotes.prepared: made ready, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder before the deletion
TT = teetotal; removed, leaving BRUNEE to rearrange

annotation.surface: With the non-drinker gone, a dark-haired woman made something with rye whiskey.
annotation.walkthrough: Rye suggests whiskey, and the missing teetotaller supports it; here rye is the bread. A Reuben is an American deli sandwich of corned beef, sauerkraut and Swiss cheese on rye.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning description: the sandwich is defined by the rye bread it comes on, not by its filling.

entries.clue: Grit that's used for storing wine (6)

blocks.note: British slang for courage
the glass container that wine is kept in

annotation.surface: Sand or gravel used in the wine cellar.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang bottle means nerve or courage: to 'lose your bottle' is to lose your nerve.
annotation.definitionFit: Grit is courage, which Britons call bottle; a bottle also holds wine.

entries.clue: Clown to stagger back: source of clip-clop sounds? (8)

annotation.walkthrough: Clapped-together coconut half shells are the classic sound effect for horses' hooves, famously in Monty Python and the Holy Grail.
annotation.definitionFit: Coconut shells banged together make a clip-clop sound.

entries.clue: Characteristic of Leicester ...? How to characterise some grins? (6)

a broad, forced smile, as when saying 'cheese' for a photo

annotation.walkthrough: Leicester reads as the English city; here it is Red Leicester, a hard orange cheese.
annotation.definitionFit: Cheesy means like cheese, and a cheesy grin is wide and exaggerated.

entries.clue: Put lid on whisky (6)

whisky distilled in Scotland

annotation.surface: Capping a bottle of whisky.

annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb meaning to end or suppress (an idiom 'put the lid on' matches), and the ordinary name for Scottish whisky.

entries.clue: Everyman 'a hilarious person', did you say? That's ... sweet (3,5)

entries.clue: Northern Europeans' roots (6)
